Dua Lipa and Callum Turner LIVE wedding updates: Couple say 'I do' as famous singer serenades them

News.title: Hegseth launches attack on Europe over migration 'invasion' during D-Day speech
News.content:
Hegseth launches attack on Europe over migration 'invasion' during D-Day speech

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has claimed that European nations are facing an 'invasion' by migrants when the statistics across Europe show a sharp decline in arrivals by small boat

View 3 Images Pete Hegseth made a speech at the US cemetery to commemorate the 82nd anniversary of the D-Day landings (Image: AP Photo/Jeremias Gonzalez)

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has falsely claimed that European nations are facing an "invasion" of migrants - a day after Vice-President JD Vance linked the murder of Henry Nowak to what he called a "mass invasion of migrants".

‌



Hegseth made the extraordinary remarks at the Normandy American Cemetery in north-west France commemorating the 82nd anniversary of D-Day, when Allied forces landed on beaches to liberate Nazi-occupied France on June 6, 1944.

‌



"Sadly, today, different European beaches are stormed by different dangerous ideologies," Hegseth said. "Beaches in Spain, in Italy, in Greece and Bulgaria. Boats and men arrive. When will European capitals do something about that invasion?"

‌



His remarks come despite official figures showing irregular migration has fallen sharply since its peak during the 2015 refugee crisis. In Greece, arrivals by small boat have fallen from 856,723 in 2015 to 41,696 in 2025 - a 95 per cent drop. In Italy, arrivals have fallen from 153,842 in 2015 to 66,316 in 2025 - a 56.9 per cent decrease.

View 3 Images Pete Hegseth attended a ceremony at the US cemetery to commemorate the 82nd anniversary of the D-Day landings in Normandy, France (Image: AP Photo/Jeremias Gonzalez)

In the UK, net migration has also fallen to its lowest level since the Covid-19 pandemic and is now 82 per cent below its record peak in 2023. It stood at an estimated 171,000 in the year to December 2025 - down nearly half (48.3 per cent) from 331,000 the year to December 2024.

‌



The latest figure is the lowest figure for any 12-month period since the year to March 2021, when it stood at 132,000. Net migration is also down 82 per cent from the record high of 944,000 in the year to March 2023.

Around 36,000 people arrived by small boat in the year ending May 31, 2026 - 13 per cent less than in the same period the year before, according to the Migration Observatory at the University of Oxford.

Hegseth's remarks came after US Vice-President JD Vance wrote on X on Friday that there should be "righteous anger" in response to the murder of Henry Nowak, which he partly blamed on "the mass invasion of migrants".

‌



His comments triggered a response from Downing Street, which hit out at "people trying to interfere in our democracy and seeking to stir up division on our streets" over Mr Nowak’s case.

View 3 Images Downing Street urged US politicians to respect the request from Henry Nowak’s family not to use his death to fuel division (Image: Yui Mok/PA Wire)

The 18-year-old student was handcuffed by police officers as he lay dying after his killer, Vickrum Digwa, claimed he had been the victim of a racist attack. The Crown Prosecution Service has confirmed that Digwa was born in Britain.

‌



A No10 spokesperson said: "In recent days we have seen people trying to interfere in our democracy and seeking to stir up division on our streets.

"The Nowak family are grieving after Henry’s horrific murder. They have said they do not want his death to be used to create further division, hatred or tension. We should be respecting their wishes. Our politics should bring people together even in the most terrible of circumstances. That is who we are as a country."

Vance's comments came after the US State Department linked "two-tier policing" to Mr Nowak’s death, echoing the claim made by Reform UK leader Nigel Farage during PMQs on Wednesday.

Article continues below

The department said: "Ideological conditioning and two-tiered policing are glaring symptoms of civilizational decline. They must be rejected across the West. The United States sends our condolences to the family of Henry Nowak and the people of the United Kingdom at this troubling time."

Downing Street has rejected "any suggestion of two-tier policing across the United Kingdom".

News.title: Iran war live: US 'lacks will to reduce tensions'
News.content:
Trump said that Iran has "no choice" but to agree to a deal

Donald Trump said he remains confident Iran will eventually agree to a deal to end the war, insisting its leaders have 'no choice' but to do so

Iran’s Foreign Ministry has said the US "lacks the will to reduce tensions and return to the path of stability" and warned that its "adventurist actions" are putting regional security at risk.

In a statement, the ministry condemned the US attack on its coastal radar and surveillance facilities in the Sirik region and Qeshm Island, the semi-official Mehr News Agency reported.

Donald Trump said on Friday that Iran's leaders have not yet agreed to a deal to end the war because they're "proud" but predicted Tehran would ultimately do so because "they've got no choice". It came after the US military shot down four Iranian drones heading towards the Strait of Hormuz as well as Kuwait and Bahrain. The US retaliated by striking Iranian coastal surveillance radar sites.

The US continues to enforce a blockade on Iranian ports while Tehran is also limiting shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

News.title: Peter Phillips and Harriet Sperling wedding live: Beatrice and Eugenie 'determined in brave move'
News.content:
Peter Phillips, the son of Princess Anne, has married NHS nurse Harriet Sperling in a church ceremony in Gloucestershire today, with senior royals including the King and the Prince and Princess of Wales attending

Peter Phillips has married Harriet Sperling with the Royal Family coming out in force to celebrate the wedding, with Princesses Beatrice and Eugenie making a "brave" appearance.

Nearly all senior royals descended on the small village of Kemble, near Cirencester in Gloucestershire, for the private nuptials, including the Prince and Princess of Wales, the Duke and Duchess of Edinburgh and the King and Queen. Also there were Princesses Beatrice and Eugenie. It is the first time they have been included in a large Royal Family gathering since the arrest of their father Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor. However, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle did not attend.

According to former BBC royal correspondent Jennie Bond, Beatrice and Eugenie's were "brave to show up", adding that "it can't have been easy for them". She added that the sisters appeared to keep a "low profile" as Jennie said they were "determined not to draw any of the limelight from the bride and groom."

The bride stunned in a lace gown by designer Emilia Wickstead, which she teamed with the Pragnell family tiara. After the ceremony, the newlyweds posed for photographers before they were whisked to their wedding reception at Gatcombe Park.

Mr Phillips, the King’s nephew, William and Harry’s first cousin and the brother of Zara Tindall, is the son of Anne and her first husband Captain Mark Phillips. He split from his first wife Autumn in 2020 after 12 years of marriage and shares custody of their two children.

News.title: Kim Jong Un parades teen successor daughter around naval destroyer as he reveals nuclear warship plans
News.content:
Kim Jong Un parades teen successor daughter around naval destroyer as he reveals nuclear warship plans

Kim Jong Un and his teenage daughter were snapped among military officials on a chilling warship days before a visit from China's Xi Jinping

View 3 Images Kim Jong Un and his daughter Kim Ju Ae on the naval destroyer (Image: KCNA VIA KNS/AFP via Getty Images)

North Korea's Kim Jong Un has brought his teenage daughter along with him to another military visit, with the pair viewing the dictator's newest warship.

‌



His daughter Kim Ju Ae, who is believed to be 13 years old, was snapped with her dad as they visited the 5,000-tonne destroyer Kang Kon on Thursday, as it underwent capability tests. This was another example of the North Korean dictator taking his eventual successor with him to view his growing list of military vessels and machines.

‌



While showing off his teen successor on yet another visit, Jong Un also revealed his plans to develop a terrifying "secret underwater weapons".

‌



Kim Jong-Un shows off new nuke factory as he sends horror threat to West READ MORE :

View 3 Images The dictator and his teen daughter on a tour of the 'Kang Kyon' (Image: KCNA VIA KNS/AFP via Getty Images)

These chilling pictures on the warship and threats of new deadly weapons comes as Chinese leader Xi Jinping is set to visit North Korea next week, which would be his first visit to the neighbouring ally since 2019. In the past year, Jong Un has been trying to improve ties with China, the North's biggest trading partner and provider of aid.

Mr Xi will make a state visit from Monday to Tuesday, Chinese and North Korean state media said. His last visit was in June 2019. The North Korean dictator announced his plans to accelerate efforts to develop a nuclear-armed naval fleet and make his "secret underwater weapons" while being snapped with his young daughter.

‌



View 3 Images The 5,000-tonne destroyer Kang Kon at sea (Image: KCNA VIA KNS/AFP via Getty Images)

The teenager stood close to her dad as he was seen talking to military officials and looking at the command centre in his destroyer. Ju Ae was also snapped pointing something out to her dad as the two looked out at the sea during the visit to the warship.

Jong Un and Ju Ae toured the vessel and the dictator was quoted calling for "rapidly developing" naval forces capable of playing a larger role in the country's nuclear deterrent. He also sent a chilling warning to his enemies in the West and nearby by saying those forces needed to be able to deal a "deadly blow at the enemy any moment under the water or on the water," state media reported.

Article continues below

Jong Un also outlined a new five-year defence plan which includes building larger 10,000-ton-class destroyers and developing unspecified "underwater secret weapons." State media outlet Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) did not report any direct remarks by Kim about Washington or Seoul during his visit.

Xi Jinping will visit North Korea in a trip that will advance ties and strengthen regional peace and stability, a Chinese spokesperson said. Foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said: "The traditional friendly and cooperative relations between China and the DPRK have continued to develop in a sound and stable manner, bringing tangible benefits to both countries and their peoples."

The trip is coming just a few weeks after Mr Xi hosted US president Donald Trump and Russian leader Vladimir Putin in quick succession in Beijing. North Korea's nuclear weapons programme has long been a major concern for the United States, which opposes it. The UN has imposed economic sanctions on North Korea because of its nuclear and missile development.

News.title: Massive blaze destroys dozens of buses destroyed in suspected arson attack
News.content:
Massive blaze destroys dozens of buses destroyed in suspected arson attack

Fire crews raced to the scene in Muckingford Road, Linford, in Essex, shortly before 7pm on Friday after flames engulfed a number of vehicles parked at the site

View 3 Images The bus depot was hit in a suspected arson attack (Image: Essex Police)

Dozens of double-decker buses have been destroyed after a huge fire tore through a bus storage yard.

‌



Fire crews raced to the scene in Muckingford Road, Linford, in Essex, shortly before 7pm on Friday after flames engulfed a number of vehicles parked at the site. When firefighters arrived they found the blaze rapidly spreading between buses in the yard, prompting a major emergency response.

‌



Crews battled for hours to bring the fire under control and by 9pm the incident had been scaled back, with two fire engines remaining at the scene to tackle hotspots and make the area safe. Essex County Fire and Rescue Service said around 36 buses were destroyed in the blaze.

‌



Station Manager Lee Hurst described the incident as "significant and challenging".

View 3 Images Fire and rescue at the scene (Image: Essex fire and rescue)

He said: "This was a significant and challenging incident involving a large number of vehicles. Thanks to the hard work and professionalism of our firefighters, supported by Essex Police, utility providers and local farmers, we were able to bring the fire under control and prevent further spread.

‌



"I would like to thank all of the partner agencies and members of the local community who assisted us throughout the incident."

Following an investigation, fire service officials concluded the blaze had been started deliberately.

Mr Hurst added: "The fire investigation has determined that the fire was started deliberately.

‌



"Anyone with information about how the fire started, or who may have seen suspicious activity in the area before the incident, is urged to contact FireStoppers anonymously."

Essex Police confirmed officers attended the scene alongside firefighters and are treating the incident as suspected arson.

View 3 Images Essex Police confirmed officers attended the scene alongside firefighters (Image: Essex fire and rescue)

‌



A spokesperson said: "We're investigating an incident in Linford which led to damage being caused to a number of buses. Alongside colleagues at Essex County Fire and Rescue, we attended a fire at a vehicle storage area in Muckingford Road shortly before 7pm on Friday 5 June.

"At this stage it is being treated as a suspected arson. We are working closely with fire service colleagues to establish the cause of the fire."

Road closures were put in place while emergency services tackled the blaze but were lifted shortly after 9pm when work at the scene concluded.

Article continues below

No arrests have been made and detectives said they are pursuing a number of lines of inquiry.

Anyone with information is urged to contact Essex Police online, through its live chat service, or by calling 101 quoting incident 1206 of June 5.

News.title: Mum-of-five in coma after contracting sepsis in Gran Canaria as family desperate to get her 'home with babies'
News.content:
Mum-of-five in coma after contracting sepsis in Gran Canaria as family desperate to get her 'home with babies'

Emily Casey, 34, from Wirral, was put into an induced coma after falling ill with pneumonia and sepsis on holiday in Gran Canaria with her husband Jamie and their five children, aged one to 13 — her family are desperately raising £50,000 for a medical flight home

View 2 Images Mum Emily Casey, 34, took ill while on holiday with her husband Jamie and their five children (Image: Jamie Casey)

The family of a mum-of-five who is stuck in hospital in Gran Canaria after contracting sepsis have said they "just want to get her home to her babies."

‌



Emily Casey, 34, was placed into a coma after falling ill while on holiday in the Canary Islands with her husband Jamie Casey and their five children. On Wednesday, May 13, merely three days after the family, from Wirral, travelled to the island, Emily began experiencing breathing difficulties and was rushed straight to a local hospital.

‌



She'd recently made a full recovery from pneumonia, so medics initially suspected she had developed a blood clot in her lung.

‌



View 2 Images Four of Jamie and Emily's young children while on holiday in Gran Canaria (Image: Jamie Casey)

Brit tourist collapses and dies in Greece while taking sick wife to hospital READ MORE :

A CT scan was carried out and the mum was informed the pneumonia had come back, reports the Liverpool Echo. Doctors revealed one of her lungs was "full of fluid," which would require draining.

Jamie headed back to the family's hotel to care for their five children that evening. Throughout the night he rang and texted Emily repeatedly to ensure she was alright while their children slept, but received no reply.

‌



The following morning Jamie hurried back to the hospital, where he discovered his wife was in an induced coma on a life support machine. In a panic, Jamie contacted their relatives back in the UK and Emily's mum travelled to Gran Canaria to assist in looking after her.

When their holiday concluded on Tuesday, 19 May Jamie returned to Liverpool with their children to sort out childcare arrangements. He travelled back to Gran Canaria days afterwards to remain at his wife's bedside.

When he returned, he was devastated to learn that his wife had developed sepsis. The family received further dire news that Emily's condition had "gone backwards", with scans showing pneumonia had "taken over her lungs again," and sepsis now present in her bloodstream.

Article continues below

More than three weeks on, Emily remains stranded in hospital in Gran Canaria. Family member Kevin Magee, who first reached out to the ECHO, revealed she was conscious but "in and out of sedation."

He stressed that the family "need to get her home to her babies," - Summer, 13, Oscar, 11, Isabelle, seven, Sophia, four and Willow, one. The family are "desperately" appealing for support to bring Emily back home and must raise £50,000 to fund a medical flight back to the UK.

A GoFundMe page has been set up in Emily's name. If you wish to help, you can make a donation online.

News.title: West Ham joint chairman David Sullivan steps down after 'serious' historical allegations
News.content:
West Ham United co-owner David Sullivan has stepped down from his position as joint chairman of the club with immediate effect following a joint investigation by BBC Panorama and the Times newspaper into his behaviour.

The BBC said Panorama's story is due to be broadcast and published on Monday.

The Hammers said they had "been made aware of the impending publication of serious historic allegations" concerning Sullivan.

In a statement of his own, the 77-year-old said a "small number of improper conduct claims" have been made against him, adding: "I categorically deny these claims."

He said the "decades-old allegations concerning my personal life" are "factually incorrect and entirely false".

Sullivan, who had held the role for 16 years, said he stepped down "to apply my full energy and attention on fighting these false allegations".

Sullivan also said he plans to sue the BBC for libel "along with any other media outlet that repeats any libellous allegations".

The Hammers were relegated from the Premier League at the end of the 2025-26 season after finishing 18th.

"At what is already a challenging and important time for the club, I refuse to allow personal matters concerning me to become an unnecessary distraction or a source of instability," added Sullivan, who has also resigned as a director.

"Therefore, after very careful consideration and with a heavy heart, I have decided to resign."

In a club statement, West Ham said Sullivan has denied any "illegal conduct" and is leaving "in order to avoid disruption to the club while he addresses the matter privately".

Sullivan has been the club's largest single shareholder since the death of his business partner David Gold in January 2023, which left him with a 38.8% stake.

Sullivan and Gold became joint chairmen of West Ham when they completed their takeover of the club in January 2010.

"It is understood none of the allegations relate to West Ham United or any of its operations," said West Ham.

"Interim chief executive officer Karim Virani, reporting into the current board of directors, will continue to be responsible for leading the club's day-to-day operations.

"The club will provide an update on the future structure of the board of directors in due course, but will make no further comment at this time."

President Donald Trump marked the 82nd anniversary of D-Day, when the Allied powers stormed the beaches of Normandy during World War II, by sharing artificial intelligence-generated content that took aim at a range of his perceived opponents.

Saturday morning, the president shared an AI music video set to the song “Trump,” created by New York congressional candidate Anthony Constantino, who he recently endorsed. The video, which aimed to show admiration of Trump from around the world, featured clips of the president riding a lion, sharing a meal with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and at the UFC Freedom 250 cage fight at the White House. All the while, a house backing track repeats the line: "Everywhere I go, they love Donald Donald Trump.”

It was the only post on Trump’s Truth Social account for several hours on June 6 until he bragged about the new Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and then shared an AI-generated image of the Obama Presidential Library deteriorating, surrounded by homeless encampments and with a large pile of garbage on top of the structure.

“The Barack Hussein Obama Library, in 10 years, when fully matured!” Trump wrote.

But the U.S. president did not post anything on Truth Social marking the anniversary of D-Day, and continued in the afternoon to mock what appeared to be Rosie O'Donnell and accused Judge Richard Leon, who temporarily halted above ground construction of the White House ballroom, of “putting our Country in danger.”

open image in gallery President Donald Trump posted an AI-generated music video featuring clips of himself being celebrated worldwide on Truth Social Saturday ( realDonaldTrump / Truth Social )

Other world leaders, such as Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and U.K. Prime Minister Keir Starmer, acknowledged the day on social media.

Trump has acknowledged D-Day in previous years. In 2024, he posted a video of himself virtually chatting with D-Day heroes in addition to a statement acknowledging soldiers who died. In 2023, he posted a video montage of D-Day, paid for by his re-election campaign.

Members of the Trump administration and federal departments also marked D-Day with social media posts remembering those who fought in the battle. Even the White House official X page posted in remembrance of those who gave their lives on June 6, 1944.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who attended a D-Day commemoration in France over the weekend, spoke about the anniversary but also tied it to the current administration’s fraught relationship with Europe’s approach to immigration.

open image in gallery President Trump shared an AI-generated post depicting the Obama Presidential Library as deteriorated and covered in garbage on D-Day ( realDonaldTrump / Truth Social )

"Sadly, today, different European beaches are stormed by different, dangerous ideologies,” Hegseth said Saturday. “Beaches in Spain, Italy, Greece and Bulgaria, boats and men arrive."

“When will European capitals do something about that invasion? Or is it too late?” he added. “I pray not, and I believe not.”

The defense secretary’s comments mirror statements Trump has made in the past, criticizing European leaders for not taking a more hardline approach to immigration.

In his second term, the president has been more critical of U.S. allies, particularly part of NATO, for relying too heavily on the U.S. for military support. He’s accused NATO allies of not supporting the US, particularly for his war with Iran.

Clashes between demonstrators and law enforcement outside a New Jersey immigration detention center since late May have become the latest flashpoint for protests against President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown.

More than 80 people have been arrested following a series of protests outside Delaney Hall in Newark, where demonstrators say they are showing up in solidarity with detainees inside over accusations of poor living conditions.

The Trump administration has defended the treatment given to detainees at the 1,000-bed facility.

Here's what to know:

Accusations of neglect at Delaney Hall

The facility is owned by Geo Group, a private prison contractor that runs multiple detention centers across the country.

Detainees launched a hunger strike last month, according Cosecha, an immigrant advocacy group. They issued a number of handwritten letters from inside with their demands, including improved living conditions and better medical care, as they say some are being denied medication.

Detainees across the country have alleged medical neglect for serious and chronic conditions, and they have announced hunger strikes at other facilities.

The Delaney Hall detainees say they are being given moldy and expired food, some of it with maggots, and are housed in overcrowded cells that lack air conditioning. Democratic members of Congress from New York City visited the facility early in the protests and said the detainees' accounts are credible.

Trump administration defends conditions

President Donald Trump and his deputies have defended the center’s operations and denied there is any hunger strike, abuse or poor conditions inside.

“The fact is, we’re giving them the calories they want,” Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said recently. “This isn’t Holiday Inn.”

Tom Homan, Trump’s border czar, praised the food after a recent visit. “The spaghetti was good,” he told CBS News.

GEO Group has dismissed the criticisms as “a politically motivated campaign by outside groups to dismantle ICE and federal immigration detention by targeting the government’s facility contractors.”

Arrests and protesters trying to stop vehicles

The protesters, some wearing gas masks and helmets, have used traffic cones, trash cans and other items as makeshift shields, and they tried to block vehicles from entering or leaving the facility.

Acting U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche shared images online of bloody wounds and bruises sustained by officers with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

Videos on social media show officers in riot gear deploying tear gas and using batons to beat back the demonstrators. Some videos have shown police on horseback marching into the crowds.

On Friday night, ICE officers arrested four on charges of assaulting law enforcement officers, obstruction and threats, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said on X. Newark police, meanwhile, said they a Seattle man was charged with criminal mischief for smashing car windows.

"No one has the right to come into our city, destroy personal property, or incite violence,” Newark Public Safety Director Emanuel Miranda posted on social media. “Think twice before coming to Newark with any other agenda than to protest peacefully.”

One law enforcement official was charged with stealing $10,000 worth of camera equipment from an Associated Press photojournalist who had been injured while covering the standoff. The journalist, Angelina Katsanis, was struck in the knee by a wood beam during a clash between police and demonstrators. She sought medical attention and used a geo-tracking device to trace her missing gear to his home, the state’s attorney general said Thursday.

New Jersey leaders and local officials take action

Democratic Gov. Mikie Sherrill was initially reluctant to intervene in the growing protests. But as the violence intensified, she declared the situation had “grown unsafe” and “unacceptable” and called in the state police to restore order.

State troopers set up designated protest zones and vehicle checkpoints as ICE officers who had been stationed in front of the detention center agreed to stand down.

Newark Mayor Ras Baraka, meanwhile, imposed a 9 p.m. curfew and sent in city police to enforce it.

But just a week later, the Democrat declared the city would be scaling back its police presence, saying arrests had dropped and he was reluctant to continue spending tax dollars to guard a privately owned facility.

The state’s attorney general this week filed a lawsuit against Geo Group, alleging the facility denied state health inspectors “full access” to investigate allegations.

Veteran 60 Minutes correspondent Scott Pelley has spoken out again following his firing from CBS.

Pelley was fired Wednesday after reportedly accusing CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss of “murdering” the top news program.

The journalist, 68, shared a new Instagram post Saturday thanking his fans for their support in the days since he received a termination letter from Nick Bilton, the new executive producer of 60 Minutes.

“To all of you who have been so kind, you are the wind in my sails. So deeply grateful,” he captioned the photo of himself out on the water.

The post has amassed over 33,000 likes and hundreds of likes within hours of being shared by Pelley.

Pelley served as the show’s managing editor and anchor, and had been a 60 Minutes correspondent for 22 years. He spent 37 years at CBS News, saying in an initial statement that he leaves with “a heart brimming with gratitude.”

He was sent a termination letter by 60 Minutes’ new executive producer, Nick Bilton, whom the journalist said had “slender” qualifications for the job.

In a note that Bilton sent to Pelley alongside his formal termination letter, which circulated on social media Tuesday night, the new 60 Minutes chief said Pelley had set up an “ambush.”

“Yesterday, you hijacked my first meeting with staff to disparage me, my qualifications, and my intentions with remarkable incivility and contempt,” Bilton wrote in the note.

Bilton had tried to reassure 60 Minutes staff at Monday’s meeting that the program “is going to stay exactly like it is for now,” and that “Bari loves this institution,” according to The New York Times, which obtained an audio recording of the tense exchange.

Veteran ‘60 Minutes’ correspondent Scott Pelley has been fired after accusing CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss of 'murdering' the top news program ( AFP/Getty )

“She is murdering 60 Minutes. She does not love this place. She was brought in to kill it, and she’s been doing exactly that,” Pelley reportedly fired back.

“She has no qualifications for her job; you have slender qualifications for this job,” he added.

Weiss, who founded the “anti-woke” media outlet The Free Press, was appointed as the network’s editor-in-chief last October after billionaire David Ellison, who has reported ties to President Donald Trump, took over CBS’s parent company, Paramount.

The CBS News boss has faced scrutiny since being appointed, particularly over her decision to pull a 60 Minutes segment about Venezuelan migrants sent by the Trump administration to CECOT, an El Salvadoran prison accused of having inhumane conditions. The segment aired nearly one month later.

Simone Biles has revealed she’s in the midst of recovering after a recent health scare.

The Olympic gymnast, 29, posted a statement Saturday on her Instagram Story, alongside a picture of multiple hospital bracelets on her wrist. However, she did not disclose what landed her in the hospital.

“I’m not one to normally share things like this because I value privacy in today’s age. But almost dying wasn’t on my bingo card earlier this week,” she wrote.

“This was one of, if not the scariest experience of my life. Especially since Jonathan [Owens] was in Indy for practices,” she continued, referring to her husband’s preseason NFL training for the Indianapolis Colts.

Biles concluded: “I’ve been in bed resting this week, I’ll explain sooner or later, but s/o to my close circle who reached out, checked in, visited or sent flowers. Love y’all.”

open image in gallery ‘I’m not one to normally share things like this because I value privacy in today’s age. But almost dying wasn’t on my bingo card earlier this week,’ Biles wrote on Instagram ( @simonebiles / Instagram )

open image in gallery Biles called the recent health issue the ‘scariest experience’ of her life ( Getty Images )

“I’ll be here,” she captioned another picture of her bed, alongside a screenshot of a monitor that read her current resting heart rate, 126 beats per minute.

The Independent has contacted a representative for Biles for comment.

Biles has previously spoken out about navigating health conditions throughout her career. Last year, she recalled how competing in the 2024 Paris Olympics, where she won three gold medals and one silver, took a toll on her body.

“I went back to the village, took the elevator, and my body literally collapsed,” she told L'Equipe, the Associated Press’s French sports outlet, in April 2025. “I was sick for 10 days.”

“The other day, we were sprinting in the garden with friends,” she added. “I had aches and pains for three days.”

Biles withdrew from some of the finals events during the 2021 Summer Olympics after suffering from “twisties,” a condition in which athletes experience a loss of spatial awareness mid-air, leaving them at risk of injury when they land.

“It doesn’t feel comfortable, I have no idea where I am, but I’m twisting, praying I land on my feet,” she said of the condition on a 2024 episode of the Call Her Daddy podcast. “I felt like I was fighting my body and my mind to do these tricks.”

After she changed the difficulty of her rotation midair — correcting her body position to avoid an accident — there was speculation about what might have been causing her struggles. However, she insisted that she didn’t have a physical issue, adding, “No, no injury, thankfully. That’s why I took a step back, because I didn’t want to do something silly out there and get injured.”

News.content:

Texas Gov. Greg Abbott has voiced significant concern over delays in constructing a new facility crucial for combating the New World screwworm fly, whose flesh-eating larvae pose a renewed threat to the nation's $113 billion cattle industry.

The governor warned on Friday that the factory, designed to breed sterile flies, is not expected to commence operations for over a year, a timeline he deems unacceptable given the recent re-emergence of the pest.

Abbott pledged Texas's full support to the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) to expedite the $750 million breeding facility's construction near Edinburg, Texas, approximately 20 miles north of the U.S.-Mexico border.

He indicated the state is prepared to commit its own funds to ensure construction proceeds "24 hours a day, seven days a week." During a news conference in Austin, Abbott stressed the urgency, stating, "Without greater sterile fly production... We cannot make it through a second summer."

The USDA confirmed an infestation of New World screwworm fly larvae this week in a three-week-old calf in La Pryor, Texas, marking the first confirmed case in the state since 1966.

This location is about 100 miles southwest of San Antonio and 50 miles from the Mexican border.

( AP )

The new Texas factory is one of two USDA-funded fly-breeding facilities, with the other being a converted site in southern Mexico, which is expected to begin producing 100 million flies weekly next month.

The Texas facility, projected to be the size of two Costco stores, aims for a weekly output of up to 300 million flies.

Officials believe both factories are essential for the complete eradication of the screwworm fly from the U.S., Mexico, and Central America.

Rear Admiral Michael Schmoyer, a member of the USDA's screwworm response team, noted that the federal government has already significantly shortened planning and construction timelines.

U.S. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins expressed hope that the facility would be operational sooner than its planned November 2027 opening, though Abbott remains determined to accelerate the process further, warning that the fly "is going to spread over the course of the summer."

While an untreated screwworm infestation can be fatal to an animal, federal and state officials have been quick to emphasize that the larvae, which feed on living tissue, do not infest meat or fruit.

"There’s a food production issue, but not a food safety issue," Abbott clarified. Derrell Peel, an agribusiness professor at Oklahoma State University, suggested the beef supply is unlikely to be significantly affected unless cattle movement is severely restricted or infestations appear in concentrated areas like feedlots, which he doesn't anticipate.

He concluded, "It's probably not a major market issue." Consumers are currently facing record beef prices due to a tight cattle supply, and Peel expects prices to rise further as ranchers rebuild herds, but he stated the screwworm's arrival "doesn't change the supply fundamentals."

The New World screwworm fly was a persistent threat to U.S. cattle ranchers from the 1930s through the 1960s.

However, the strategic release of sterile flies from planes successfully eradicated the pest from the U.S. by the early 1970s, with only brief outbreaks in the Florida Keys in 2016 and a case involving a Maryland man who traveled to El Salvador last year.

Female screwworm flies mate only once in their month-long lives, and if they breed with sterile males, their eggs will not hatch after being laid in open wounds or mucous membranes of warm-blooded animals, including livestock, wildlife, pets, and humans. Following past eradication efforts, most fly-breeding facilities were shut down, leaving only one in Panama, capable of producing about 117 million flies weekly.

However, Schmoyer noted that previous eradication campaigns required approximately 500 million flies per week.

To combat the current threat, Schmoyer estimated that the USDA has already dispersed 130 million flies in Texas since January, primarily from planes, with current drops at about 4 million per week. An additional 4 million pupae (flies in the stage between larvae and adult) are being released on the ground weekly. Schmoyer explained that the USDA must be strategic in its dispersal, utilizing scientific models to predict the fly's movement.

"In essence, it’s not where the flies are today, but where they could be weeks from now," he said. Texas State Veterinarian Bud Dinges confirmed that traps have been deployed up to 120 miles from La Pryor to monitor the fly's spread.

News.title: Spike Lee gets ‘Pope’ mobile treatment in Brooklyn after New York Knicks take NBA finals lead
News.content:
Film director Spike Lee received the “Pope” mobile treatment in Brooklyn after the New York Knicks won a second game against the San Antonio Spurs in the NBA finals.

The Knicks beat the Spurs 105-104 Friday (6 June), giving them a 2-0 lead in the championship series.

Lee, widely known for being a superfan of the New York basketball team, was filmed waving to fans out of the sunroof of his car in Fort Greene, Brooklyn, following the game. Crowds cheered and sang as he slowly passed through the neighborhood.

One fan noted on social media: "They’re parading Spike Lee around Fort Greene post-Knicks win like he’s the Pope."

The Knicks will face the Spurs for Game 3 on Monday (8 June) at Madison Square Garden.

News.title: Kim Kardashian finally lands in F1 paddock but Lewis Hamilton must settle for third
News.content:
Pressure? What pressure? Antonelli is absolutely flying right now. The Italian teenager has won the last four races to establish a 43-point lead over team-mate George Russell in the drivers’ championship standings and he reacted to this pole as if he had already won the race. Which, to be fair, he may well have done. “Whoooooee,” the Italian screamed over the radio. “Yes!”

“My man,” replied his engineer Peter ‘Bono’ Bonnington. “43 milliseconds.”

Russell had tried some mind games during his media session on Thursday, saying the pressure was all on Antonelli now, with the title “his to lose”.

That is how you respond. If Antonelli converts this pole, the Italian’s lead over the Briton will start to feel gargantuan. Russell was only able to take sixth on the grid, four tenths slower than Antonelli in Q3, and looked and sounded despondent afterwards. “I don’t really know what’s going on, to be honest,” he admitted. “It’s clearly something in my driving that’s not helping the car at the moment. At the start of the season, every lap was good, it was P1 every session.”

Pushed on what that was, Russell said it was to do with getting the tyres in the right operating window. “It’s clear in the data,” he added. “But I’ve been driving in this manner my whole career. And now for whatever reason it’s not working with this car. Last year’s car, you know, Kimi was trying to drive it my way and it was also not working for him.

“It’s no excuse, it’s just a reality. I need to either work with the team to adjust my driving… or I need to find a different set-up that works for me. But it’s not clicking right now.”

News.title: Henry Slade leads Exeter into new era and brings an end to Mark McCall’s Saracens reign
News.content:
The end of an era for Saracens, as the curtain finally fell on Mark McCall’s 17-year tenure, and the beginning of a new one for their fierce rivals Exeter Chiefs, whose new-look side stormed into the Prem play-offs with this comprehensive victory.

Just a year ago, Rob Baxter’s side finished in ninth place, forcing him to fast-track his development of a new XV. Now his side will travel to Bath on Saturday hoping to book their place in the Prem final six years after their last title.

Baxter’s ability to rebuild yet another side in such a short space of time is remarkable, yet it was one of his veterans that stole the show, with Henry Slade almost single-handedly leading the charge and finishing the game as man-of-the-match thanks to a 17-point haul.

Slade was magnificent, turning back the years with an all-court performance that could see him force himself back into contention for an England spot. His last cap was against Argentina last November.

News.title: Ollie Robinson the one bright spot on rain-ravaged day at Lord’s
News.content:
At least Ollie Robinson was smiling after adding two more wickets to his match haul, which now stands at seven, and should finish with a career-best performance on his return to Test cricket.

Robinson bowled Rachin Ravindra and had Daryl Mitchell leg-before, two potentially dangerous batsmen, and the match would have been over inside three days had the weather not intervened.

Rain in England is unavoidable and part of the gamble when you buy a Test match ticket. But what you do not expect as a paying customer is for the match to be shortened by conditions that make for an imbalance between bat and ball. The match has spanned 147 overs so far and is unlikely to reach 180, the equivalent of two days’ play, because of the bowler-friendly conditions.

Batsmen have struggled to cope with uneven bounce and a pitch that has offered a lot of movement off the seam. For England this is the third Test match in six that a match has barely lasted two days’ worth of cricket.

It has not quite been a lottery. New Zealand had their chances and dropped catches or failed to use their reviews wisely to give England a helping hand. England also lost the toss but showed some grit in difficult circumstances to put themselves in a winning position. The pitch played perfectly into the hands of English seamers who have shown off their skills. Robinson and Gus Atkinson bowled with great accuracy while Josh Tongue continued his development from the Ashes and is arguably the best bowler in the side now.

News.title: Mirra Andreeva becomes first Russian major winner since start of Ukraine war
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Maja Chwalinska v Mirra Andreeva in the women’s French Open final.

What a tantalising match-up this promises to be. Poland’s Chwalinksa, the world number 114 has stunned Roland Garros these past two weeks after coming through qualifying and is one win away from a fairytale triumph.

If she succeeds, she will write her name into the history books by becoming only the second qualifier in the Open Era to win a major after Emma Raducanu’s 2021 US Open victory. It would also provide a fitting ending to a French Open that has been defined by chaos and shock results.

Less than a week ago, Chwalinska was jokingly asking for help paying for a hotel room, but as she sank onto the red brick dust of Philippe-Chatrier after clinching a place in the final, she tripled her career earnings during her time in the French capital.

“Let’s not pretend someone expected it,” she said after her 7-6, 6-4 semi-final win over Diana Shnaider. “I was outside the top 100, and now I’m in the finals of a grand slam, so I feel like it’s a big thing. So it’s hard to process it.”

But 19-year-old Andreeva, the world number eight, stands in the Pole’s way. Should the in-form teenager come out on top this afternoon, she will be the first Russian to win a major since her country’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

A semi-finalist at Roland Garros two years ago, Andreeva would also become the third-youngest first-time Grand Slam champion this century, after Maria Sharapova and Raducanu.

Her first Grand Slam appearance was always going to come sooner rather than later. Ever since she burst on to the scene as a 16-year-old and reached the Wimbledon fourth round, Andreeva has been one of the brightest young stars in the sport.

However this one pans out it promises to be an intriguing contest between a player who has emerged from relative obscurity or an established teenage star who seems born for the big stage.

News.title: Kevin McCloud: ‘You could slap me in the face with a design trend and I wouldn’t know what it was’
News.content:
What would you recommend installing to make your home more sustainable?

Helen, North West

Insulation. It doesn’t matter what the insulation is. You can put it in the most disgusting petrochemical insulation ever invented but it will probably pay for itself within ten days.

What was the first thing you did to redesign your first property?

Mary-Grace, East of England

The first house I lived in was a two-up, two-down, so we couldn’t do much with it and we didn’t have any money. So I remember it had an Artex ceiling in the kitchen, which was foul. And so rather than try and rip it off, the builder said it was easy to batten over it and stick another ceiling underneath it. To this day, it probably still has two ceilings.

Then we put trendy cork tiling down, and I tiled over the kitchen worktop with some ceramic tiles. It was more of a rehash and resurfacing of the building. All the old stuff was still underneath, including that really tacky 70s kitchen.

Is there any retro style that you’d like to see make a comeback?

Mark, London

I’d really like to see modernism come back. Brutalism, is an evolution of that same idea. I’m all for a bit of rigour and architecture and design that reflects the time we’re in.

Am I interested in seeing new fourteenth-century plague pit architecture and design? No. Not really. Do I want to see the eighteenth-century – a century of cholera and bad dentistry – in my interiors? No. I want to feel that I’m living in the modern age. I want to feel that I’m living in a sustainable 21st-century world.

What are the biggest changes you’ve noticed over the years running the show?

Peter, London

Architecture is so slow that by the time you’ve been through planning and got the thing built, whatever you thought might have been fashionable then is now not. So forget it.

What I’ve noticed over the past 25 years, as we came into this century, is a change from a point where we were almost trying to reproduce and regurgitate the twentieth century, in the early years, trying to figure out what this new language would be in building and design.

What has happened is that we’ve started revisiting the buildings of the 1970s. I see that emerging more and more with soft forms, curves and arches and use of softer materials. We’re seeing more organic forms with sustainability, with highly insulated buildings, a huge amount of timber, a huge amount of engineered timber, glulam beams, Parallam beams, all kinds of structural timber that’s replacing steel and concrete, as well as straightforward walls.

And I think that’s devoutly to be wished. It feels to me as though our language for this century is going to be a far more sensitive one, a far less material-intensive one, one that is more sustainable and more gentle and a little bit more rounded.

Why are modern houses low quality?

Norman, Wales

Modern houses are really low quality in the UK because we have a delivery system based on the principle of delivering very large profits to shareholders. It’s almost the only country in Europe where volume housing places profits above quality.

It stems from ideas grown in the 1980s in politics about ownership and treating our homes as assets, as investments for shareholders and as well as for homeowners, as opposed to treating housing as a social good, a foundation of civilisation.

The UN describes housing as a basic human right, not a commodity. So I think the problem in the UK is treating our housing essentially as commoditised objects, which we buy and sell and make money on and therefore build as cheaply as possible.

It’s a complicated landscape and it’s not easy to fix at all. But if you look at other European models, they’re far more diverse. There’s much more choice of tenure, of typology, of mixing the social and the private, of model and architectural style, of greater choice of builder. You can, if you’re living in Austria, choose probably from three important, good local builders in the town where you live, and you’ll be building a house probably made out of the forest that’s over there on the mountain.

Who has been most influential in your career?

Sheila, South East

There have been so many kind and helpful people. None of us get through life by ourselves. None of us get through life by rushing or hurrying or trying to be too independent. I think actually relying on great people and taking advice and support from them is one thing I’ve learned reluctantly over my life.

I say reluctantly because when I was much younger, I was independent and determined. I thought I could do everything. I soon realised you just don’t and can’t.

News.title: England in sight of uplifting win after key Williamson wicket
News.content:
New Zealand helped with some poor catching, shoddy batting and decision-making. Harry Brook’s first-innings fifty and Gay’s 57 on day two were both built on missed opportunities. Brook was dropped twice, Gay edged between first and second slip on 20 and New Zealand failed to review a not out leg-before when he had 24 that would have been overturned by Hawk-Eye. They dropped Ben Duckett on 12 and he scored 33, and Jacob Bethell on eight, and while he did not make a big score, he batted on for another half hour, preventing New Zealand from having a go at a fresh batsman before lunch.

The ghosts of Perth stalked England, whispering in their ears all day, but this time they kept their heads. After mopping up the New Zealand innings for 113 in the first hour, with Ollie Robinson adding one more to his overnight four wickets for a career-best five for 39, England reached lunch 72 for one in their second innings following the only relatively calm passage of play. It was a lead of 99 – exactly the scenario at the same stage of the opening Ashes Test in November.

Then they lost three for no runs – the heart ripped out of the batting as Ollie Pope, Joe Root and Harry Brook fell in a blaze of wild drives – and the whole Ashes project disintegrated with the ink still drying on the entry stamps in their passports.

At Lord’s, England lost four for one in 11 balls to plunge to 127 for six, the lead now only 154 and Will O’Rourke breathing menace from the Pavilion End and Nathan Smith giving nothing away from the Nursery End. It started with Gay hanging his bat out to be caught behind. O’Rourke was full and swung in late to knock over Brook leg-before on review and, first ball of the next over, Smith nipped one in off the wobble seam to pin Joe Root on the back leg.

News.title: Trump says ‘stocks should go up, not down’ amid market slump
News.content:
Donald Trump has said “stocks should go up, not down” after Wall Street was hit by a sell-off following new strong US jobs data.

Official figures on Friday revealed the US economy created twice as many jobs as had been expected last month. Non-farm payrolls rose by 172,000 in May. They were expected to rise by just 88,000.

The report fuelled a market rout on Friday, with the Dow Jones down 0.55pc, the Nasdaq falling 3pc and the S&P 500 down almost 2pc.

Investors dumped stocks on growing expectations that the strong jobs figures would prompt the Federal Reserve, America’s central bank, to lift interest rates.

Responding to the market actions, Mr Trump said: “With a great Jobs report, like just announced, stocks should go up, not down.”

“That’s the way it was for 200 years. Growth does not mean inflation! How else can a Country attain GREATNESS??? President DJT”

Traders are now betting the Fed will lift interest rates from the current range of between 3.5pc and 3.75pc to between 3.75pc and 4pc by December.

Higher interest rates would increase costs for the world’s biggest tech companies, which are currently investing huge sums into AI infrastructure using hundreds of billions worth of loans.

The market slump on Friday follows a wider sell-off in US markets this week, sparked by mounting concerns around a possible tech bubble.

Underwhelming results from Broadcom, the microchip maker, on Thursday added to investors fears that some of the world’s top tech companies may be overvalued.

It meant more than $650bn was wiped from the value of America’s microchip giants on Thursday.

Sports.title: Who is England vs New Zealand referee Natalie Simon?
Sports.content:
ENGLAND are taking on New Zealand in a pre-World Cup friendly TONIGHT.

Natalie Simon is officiating the match at the Raymond James Stadium, the home of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.





SunSport brings you the lowdown on the referee.

Who is England vs New Zealand referee Natalie Simon?

Natalie Simon is an American international referee, hailing from Louisiana.

She attended Stetson University, where she played football competitively as a forward.

Simon’s career as a referee began in 2015, when she joined the National Intercollegiate Soccer Officials Association.

The official was named Referee of the Year four years later in 2019.

In April 2022, Simon took charge of her first United States Women’s match as a centre referee.

Six months later, she officiated her maiden championship match in the NWSL between Portland Thorns and Kansas City Current.

During the same year, she became one of four American women to earn a Fifa international refereeing badge.



The following September, Simon made history by becoming the first black woman to referee an MLS match.

She took charge of the clash between the San Jose Earthquakes and Real Salt Lake.

Sports.title: Secret £500,000 England World Cup victory parade lined up if Three Lions lift trophy in US
Sports.content:
THE Government is secretly working on plans for a massive £500,000 parade if England win the World Cup, The Sun on Sunday can reveal.

Civil servants have been tasked with preparing nationwide festivities on the basis Thomas Tuchel’s side go all the way this summer.





Plans are under way for one of Britain’s biggest-ever victory marches across London in the week after the July 19 final.

The Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) is working towards a date in the days soon after that.

It comes after the Government and the FA hastily put together a parade in the capital for the Lionesses after they retained their Euros title in 2025.

Whitehall mandarins are said to have informally consulted the FA on how best to manage an estimated crowd of millions.

Just drawing up the plans has already cost tens of thousands, with officials in the process of hiring a double decker bus for the parade, a large stage area and live entertainment.

The estimated total cost is around £500,000, sources claim.

But it is seen as good value due to the expected boost to national morale with an England win.

Officials are also looking into how quickly stars including Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham can fly back from the US if the Three Lions become champs for only the second time after 1966.



It is expected the team would return one or two days after the final — giving them a short time to recover before being presented to the public as world champions.

A source said: “If England do win the World Cup and there isn’t a plan, both the Government and the FA would look stupid.”

Any parade is likely to be ­similar to the Lionesses’ victory celebrations last year, which saw 65,000 in central London.



The DCMS said: “At this stage, speculation around possible ­celebrations is premature, but of course we will celebrate success in the right way.”

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola’s close friendship with stunning TV pundit Natalie Pike revealed as pair bond over Man City interviews
Sports.content:
'LOVE YOU, PEP' Pep Guardiola’s close friendship with stunning TV pundit Natalie Pike revealed as pair bond over Man City interviews

BROADCASTER Natalie Pike helped Manchester City fans say farewell to their record-breaking boss — then shared a message telling him: “I love you, Pep.”

The pair formed a close friendship after chatting regularly for the club TV channel.





Natalie, a former model for FHM magazine, conducted Pep’s final interview on the Etihad pitch on May 24 and was snapped with him the next day at his leaving bash at the Co-op Live arena.

Afterwards 43-year-old Natalie — who also works for BBC Radio Five, talkSPORT, DAZN and Race Day TV — posted a video to her Instagram showing her and Pep sharing a celebratory hug and a kiss.

In an Instagram message referring to her success in a fantasy football league, she wrote: “Love you Pep . . . But me and fantasy football are forever.”

She and 55-year-old Pep — who is in the process of finalising his divorce from Cristina Serra, his wife and partner of more than 30 years — have been pictured numerous times in each other’s company on social media.



A source at the club said: “Natalie was doing all the presenting and does a lot of the interviews with the players and manager. They became friends.”

Lifelong City fan Natalie joined the club’s presenting team in 2011 and is a familiar face on match days at the Etihad Stadium.

She has interviewed a host of City players, legends and celebrity fans, as well as dad-of-three Pep, who separated from 53-year-old Cristina in 2024.

In front of a packed stadium following City’s last home game of the season two weeks ago, emotional Natalie told him: “What you’ve done for our football club is immeasurable. Manchester is blue because of you, Pep.”



Just a week ago she posted a short video of her spinning gleefully on the City crest, with the caption: “How life feels when you’ve spent ten years with the greatest manager of all time!”

Days after Pep announced he was leaving, Natalie told co-host Chris Sutton on Radio 5 Live: “Oh Chris, I don’t know how I’m not gonna cry about Pep.”

Later on the show, when the conversation turned to who was the best manager ever, she said: “To me, obviously, he’s the greatest football manager of all time.”



During a discussion about the reasons behind Pep’s departure from City — who are fighting FA finance charges — Sutton asked Natalie if Pep had messaged her with an explanation.

She said: “Yeah Chris, he said to my face. He’s going now because he believes it’s time.

“I think the phrase he used to me was, ‘It’s time to open the windows and let some air in now around the club’.

“I really do not believe the people that are looking for conspiracy theories here or who indeed think he’s running away. It’s ten years, ten incredible years, and it’s just his time.”

Natalie said her end-of-season interview with Pep would be the “biggest moment in my career”. She added he has a “great sense of humour” and is a Coldplay fan.



Scottish-born Natalie has co-hosted three of the team’s Premier League title-winning parades and was also at the club’s ­Christmas party.

She will be working at the World Cup this month as host of the Scotland House fanzone podcast in Boston, sponsored by Marks & Spencer.

She told supporters online: “To experience a Fifa World Cup surrounded by the Tartan Army with the @scotlandnationalteam is going to be unforgettable.”



Natalie, who lives in Cheshire, was named FHM’s High Street Honey of the year in 2004 and was a hostess on telly game show The Price is Right.

She split from husband Jamie during the pandemic and has spoken publicly about her heartbreak at the marriage breakdown.

She told the Brood magazine: “I’d never experienced loneliness or sadness like it. I think, for anyone going through a divorce, you would surround yourself with friends and family — go out and get drunk, and do things to take your mind off it.

“But I couldn’t do any of that because it was in the middle of lockdown.

“I was at rock bottom — genuinely, like real, real rock bottom.”



Pep won 20 major trophies during his ten-year reign at City.

The legendary boss is now back in his native Barcelona and plans to take a break from day-to-day management to recharge his batteries.

Just days after his departure he won the Legends Trophy golf tournament at the luxurious Emporda Golf Course near Girona.



However, Pep is not cutting ties with City completely.

He is understood to have signed up to become a global ambassador for the City Football Group, acting as a high-level technical advisor for the group’s massive network of worldwide clubs.

The club was approached for comment.

Sports.title: Why is there a pirate ship inside Raymond James Stadium during England vs New Zealand?
Sports.content:
ENGLAND take on New Zealand at the Raymond James Stadium in their first World Cup warm-up friendly.

Thomas Tuchel has two more chances to see his squad in action before their Group L opener against Croatia on June 17.



ENGLAND VS NEW ZEALAND LIVE



The huge ship at the end of the stadium has caught the attention of many fans.

SunSport brings you the lowdown on the ship below.

Why do Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a pirate ship inside Raymond James Stadium?

The Raymond James Stadium is the home of the NFL franchise, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

The Bucs stadium features a 100-foot-long Buccaneers ship behind one of the end zones.

The ship is made of concrete, with six cannons on board, four of which fire confetti and two make cannon noises after each touchdown the Bucs score.

Tampa has a history with pirates, as the city hosts the annual Gasparilla Pirate Festival, a parade that pays tribute to the legendary Jose Gaspar.



Gaspar built a pirate kingdom on the Gulf coast of Florida in the late 1700s, so when Tampa got a professional football team in 1976, they named it after the city’s pirate legend.

Why is Thomas Tuchel ‘worried’ about the England vs New Zealand pitch?

Images of tonight’s pitch at the Raymond James Stadium have gone viral and caused panic amongst England fans.

The surface was installed just seven days ago and appears to be uneven and poorly connected.

Many World Cup matches will be played in stadiums that usually have artificial surfaces, but the pitches have been relaid with grass for the tournament.



Speaking about the pitch before the friendly against New Zealand, Tuchel said: “I just saw it. It will not affect my selection.

“I heard it should be OK. We want it to be OK.

“I saw a photo that made me a little bit worried and concerned but we can always react when we are there.”

Some fans are worried that the condition of the pitch could put England’s star players at risk of injury on the eve of the World Cup.

FA ground staff are believed to be in contact with stadium bosses leading up to the clash, which kicks off at 4pm local time (9pm UK time).



One EFL groundsman who saw the dodgy pitch snaps told the Daily Mail: “That’s the giveaway that it’s only just been laid.

“Ideally you would want to leave it for the roots to form into a profile and the pitch to settle but that hasn’t happened here.

“These types of pitches are called ‘plug and play’ because they are designed to be played on in a few days.”

New Zealand trained on the surface in the lead-up to tonight’s friendly and manager Darren Bazeley said: “I think it will be fine once it gets a bit of water on it.”

Sports.title: Man Utd hopeful for summer breakthrough over stadium plans for £2billion Wembley of the North
Sports.content:
SIR JIM RATCLIFFE is confident Andy Burnham’s bid to become Prime Minister will not derail his Wembley of the North.

Manchester United are set to plough on with their new £2billion stadium, even if Greater Manchester Mayor Burnham packs his bags for Westminster.





Despite the mayor’s crucial role in the plans, United’s top brass insist his potential departure will not scupper the project.

A return to the Commons through the Makerfield by-election on June 18, means the 56-year-old will vacate his local throne.

The big Labour player has been the linchpin of the Old Trafford Regeneration Task Force.

Burnham is in regular contact with redevelopment chair Lord Seb Coe and serves as the political heavyweight needed to squeeze crucial public funding out of Whitehall.

His mission to become an MP means the stadium project could lose its chief architect in local government just as the regeneration plans hit a critical delivery phase.

Although it certainly would not hurt United’s case if a key supporter of their stadium plans takes the highest office in the country.

United chiefs hope to make a summer breakthrough in their negotiations over the land needed to build a record-breaking 100,000-seater stadium.

Freightliner, a huge rail freight business behind the Stretford End, are yet to agree to the sale of its land, where much of the stadium and its wider facilities are set to be built.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But United insiders insist the project is safe from mayoral musical chairs because the blueprint is legally binding.

The by-election was called after then-Labour MP Josh Simons stepped down, to allow Burnham to run for Parliament and mount a leadership bid on Keir Starmer.

Burnham previously said that he could use compulsory purchase powers via the development corporation to force the sale of land required for the new stadium.

Buying the necessary land next to Old Trafford has been a stumbling block, as Freightliner wants at least £400m to move out to Lancashire.



A Freightliner spokesperson told SunSport that the company is unlikely to completely vacate the site until 2031.

That is one year after Ratcliffe, 73, had initially planned his grand unveiling.

While Freightliner’s ideal new hub is lined up in a St Helens industrial park, the move remains stuck in limbo as planning permission for the expanded site faces final-stage consultations.

But Freightliner told SunSport they remain confident that planning consent can be granted by 2028.



Until United know what land they can use, they cannot settle on a final design, which is needed to work out funding.

United CEO Omar Berrada was asked about the current situation mid-week.

He said: “Hopefully we’ll have some news to share in the next few weeks or months.

“Once we’ve secured the land and we know the exact location of where the new stadium could be, we will proceed to finalise the design, which will then give us a very good understanding of the potential cost.”



United promise to foot the £2bn bill for the stadium itself, leaving public money to bankroll the surrounding mega-regeneration footprint.

The wider Trafford area project plans to unlock over 15,000 new homes, sprawling entertainment hubs, and public plazas.

The club’s debts already stand at over £1.3bn before financing for the stadium has been sought.

This week it was revealed that members of the Glazer family are weighing up options to sell their stakes, which collectively come to 70 per cent.

The six Glazer siblings face mounting accusations of hunting for outside investors simply to dodge dipping into their own pockets for the stadium bill.



SunSport reached out to the family for comment.

In January, Burnham and Trafford council leader Tom Ross both hailed a new development corporation designed to enable the stadium.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Three weeks later however, the pair issued statements hitting out at Ratcliffe’s comments on the UK being “colonised by immigrants”.

Starmer and Chancellor Rachel Reeves, who also previously expressed support for the redevelopment project, also criticised Ratcliffe, who later apologised.

Kylian Mbappe lets rip at Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi suggestion with sharp response

Kylian Mbappe has weighed in with his verdict on Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi - and the Real Madrid forward gave a measured response when asked about the duo

View 2 Images Kylian Mbappe let rip at a Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi suggestion (Image: Getty Images)

Kylian Mbappe has hit out at suggestions that the difference between Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo is 'talent' and 'hard work' - but refused to give an answer on which one he prefers.

‌



Speaking ahead of this summer's World Cup in North America, France international Mbappe was asked about the age old debate involving Ronaldo and Messi. But Mbappe, 27, who has played against both players on a number of occasions, gave a diplomatic answer and refused to chose over over the other.

‌



Mbappe, however, instead opted to attack a false narrative around both players that Messi's game is based on talent alone, while Ronaldo has gained his football ability through purely hard work.

‌



Thomas Frank makes decision on next job as ex-Tottenham boss speaks out READ MORE :

Arsenal make transfer move for PSG star who will be out of contract in days READ MORE :

He told Sorare: "Without sounding condescending, that is something only someone who hasn't played soccer would say. That isn't something a true soccer person would say.

"Because if you tell me Ronaldo lacks talent or Messi hasn't put in the work, it means you’ve never in your life laced up your boots to train day in and day out. I can't fathom lacing up your boots every day and still thinking that way. I'm speaking from the heart."

Mbappe added: "One is right-footed, the other left-footed. One is tall, the other shorter. One is stronger, the other leaner. One has better finishing, the other more vision."

‌



View 2 Images Football fans are still debating who is better between Messi and Ronaldo (Image: AFP or licensors)

Messi's playing style is defined by his low centre of gravity, excellent close control, and unparalleled football intelligence. Alongside this, the Argentine has established himself as a world-class scorer and goal creator, scoring 910 times and assisting 414 goals in his career.

Ronaldo, meanwhile, has evolved from an explosive, trick-heavy winger during his early career into one of the most lethal and complete goalscorers in football history. Indeed, the Portugal international has scored a whopping 973 goals since making his senior debut in 2002.

‌



Mbappe isn't the only player that has been quizzed on Messi and Ronaldo in recent days, with Messi's international teammate Angel Di Maria weighing in with his verdict on Friday.

"For me, Leo is better than Cristiano because he has a natural talent; he doesn't have to work constantly to match or equal someone else," the former Real Madrid star explained.

Sports.title: Arsenal make transfer move for PSG star who will be out of contract in days
Sports.content:
Arsenal make transfer move for PSG star who will be out of contract in days

Arsenal have made a move for a Paris Saint-Germain player who is set to be out of contract at the end of the June, as the Gunners look to get some transfer business in early

View 2 Images Arsenal are eyeing up a move for PSG's Emmanuel Mbemba (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal have made an approach to sign talented Paris St-Germain defender Emmanuel Mbemba on a free transfer this summer, it has been claimed.

‌



The 18-year-old has been offered a new contract by PSG but is open to a move to a top Premier League club, with training compensation set to be just over £150,000 after his contract expires at the end of June.

‌



According to the BBC, the Gunners have made 'contact' with Mbemba's representatives and outlined what the club could offer to him, making reference to William Saliba's progression when signed from Saint-Etienne.

‌



Erling Haaland to Real Madrid transfer row takes twist as response to statement issued READ MORE :

Thomas Frank makes decision on next job as ex-Tottenham boss speaks out READ MORE :

Saliba signed for Arsenal for £27million in 2019 and spent three years out on loan, first back at Saint-Etienne and then Nice and Marseille, before returning to Mikel Arteta's side for the 2022/23 season.

The Frenchman has since established a spot in Arsenal's first-choice XI alongside Gabriel Magalhaes at centre-back, making 184 appearances and helping the Gunners win the Premier League title this season.

Mbemba could replicate Saliba's progress and he is reported to 'favour' Arsenal, having seen the recent stability and success the team have had under manager Arteta's leadership across the last six years.

‌



View 2 Images Emmanuel Mbemba has been linked with a move to Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

During his chat with Arsenal, Mbemba was told he would go out on a European loan until January 2027, giving the 2008-born sensation time to seal a work permit to play in England.

While Mbemba has primarily played as a centre-back for PSG's Under 19s this season, the Gunners view him as a long-term option at left-back and succeeding Riccardo Calafiori and Piero Hincapie.

‌



Mbemba is a France youth international and has made 27 appearances for PSG's U19s this term, scoring twice. He was part of the PSG side that lost to Real Madrid in the semi-final of the UEFA Youth League.

Arsenal are expected to be active in the summer transfer window as they look to strengthen their squad after winning the Premier League title. Sandro Tonali, Eli Junior Kroupi and Julian Alvarez are among the players being linked with a move to the Emirates Stadium.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel sends Eberechi Eze message and gives heartbroken Arsenal stars reality check
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel says England’s players will “take care” of Eberechi Eze after his penalty shoot-out heartbreak.

Eze missed his spot kick in the Champions League final against Paris Saint Germain and it took Mikel Arteta to console him after Arsenal ’s devastating defeat.



Arsenal’s four players - Eze, Bukayo Saka, Noni Madueke and Declan Rice - have been given extra time off after the Champions League to recover both mentally and physically.

‌



It might hit Eze hardest of all because he missed from the spot in the shoot-out but Tuchel insists that his other players will ensure there is no hangover for the Arsenal players.

England boss Tuchel also reminded the Arsenal contingent that they have had a “great season” overall after winning the first title in 22 years and they matched the best club side in Europe in the Champions League final.

Thomas Tuchel gives England stars green light to complete blockbuster transfers READ MORE :

Tuchel said: “Of course it’s painful for Ebs but of course I will take care of it, the group will take care of him and I think the extra week they had will help a lot.

“I’m very happy that they got the title in England. I think that took a lot of weight off their shoulders and they were aware they did what they could and they were very close in the final.

‌



“I don’t think I will need to lift them. They’ve absolutely had a great season. I’m always happy to do it if I have to but they should know that a final just comes down to one or two shots in a penalty shoot-out which means it cannot be closer. At some point a winner has to be found.

“I have lost some finals in a penalty shoot-out and it’s the closest way to lose and it hurts of course, it hurts a lot to lose big finals but a penalty means you did evrything right, it couldn’t be closer.

View 3 Images Eze missed a penalty during the shootout defeat to PSG last weekend (Image: Getty Images)

“But it also means you were absolutely on the same level with maybe the best team in the world at the moment.”

‌



Arsenal’s four-strong contingent are flying in to West Palm Beach where England’ are training at the Palm Beach Gardens Tennis and Pickleball Centre.

But they are not expected to be at England’s first friendly against New Zealand which is 220 miles away in Tampa.

They will be reunited with their other England team mates when they return after the game and Tuchel has even arranged for them to be able to rewatch videos of team meetings which have been held this week.

Rice has played an exhausting amount of football while the others have also been on a rollercoaster ride after their season.

‌



Saka had a premiere of a new documentary on him in New York this week which Eze attended while the others took a break and Rice posted pictures of himself on his week off with Hollywood pal James Corden.

View 3 Images Declan Rice joined James Corden and ex-West Ham skipper James Corden

Tuchel expects the Arsenal players to be in great spirits and revealed that he has already been in touch with some of them to make them feel part of it.

Tuchel added: “I saw pictures and I heard messages already that they're happy to come, the group is waiting. We’re in good spirits, so this is normally what helps and I think they're very well aware of what they achieved this season.

‌



“I thought I would just leave them to themselves, so they could be proud of what they achieved. We spoke after their title in the Premier League, which was the big target and I think that was the main target.

"I could feel that it makes them proud, and took a weight off their shoulders and I think there is no need to be overly disappointed and to carry it into the World Cup campaign. I don't see that."

Sports.title: Defending champions Bath book home semi-final as Exeter, Leicester progress
Sports.content:
Bath secured home advantage in the Gallagher Prem play-offs after beating Leicester 24-22 at a rainswept Recreation Ground.

The reigning champions withstood a powerful Leicester challenge to nail down second place behind Northampton and will host Exeter next Saturday for a place in the final.

Tigers, meanwhile, face a testing trip to East Midlands rivals Northampton on Friday as the title race reaches its penultimate lap.

Bath had their South African prop Thomas du Toit to thank for putting them in the driving seat as he scored a hat-trick of tries, all from close range, while wing Joe Cokanasiga also touched down, with fly-half Santi Carreras kicking two conversions.

Leicester went toe-to-toe for long periods through tries by Orlando Bailey, Jack van Poortvliet and George Pearson, while James O'Connor added two conversions and a penalty.

Bath, though, were not to be denied, staying firmly on course for a third successive Prem final appearance after losing to Northampton in 2024 and beating Leicester a year ago.
